channel.title: The Darkstar — daily editions
channel.description: Daily research reporting on black holes and neutron stars.

item.title: The Darkstar — 2026-11-28: A Waveform Model for the Black Holes Between Two Familiar Extremes
item.description:
Read the 2026-11-28 edition

  • A Waveform Model for the Black Holes Between Two Familiar Extremes — An analytical model follows unequal-mass black hole pairs from inspiral through ringdown, but its strongest checks lie on either side of the intermediate regime it aims to serve.
  • A Dark Matter Halo Could Change a Black Hole’s Ringing Unevenly — In a theoretical halo model, different gravitational vibrations shift by different amounts—a more revealing signature than a simple change in pitch.
  • Why a Quantum Black Hole May Have Fewer Ways to Fade — A fixed-energy calculation challenges an infinite classical tower of damped modes and the associated prediction of unbounded growth at an extreme horizon.
  • Can a Black Hole Hide a Chaotic Collapse? — A five-dimensional construction joins a regular horizon to an interior whose geometry follows the long-sought pattern of a cosmological billiard.
  • A Black Hole Disk Model Connects Work in Kraków and Prague — The publication trail of Paweł Doruchowski, Tomasz Grewenda, David Kofroň and Patryk Mach brings together kinetic gas, magnetic fields and Kerr geometry.

item.title: The Darkstar — 2026-11-27: Can Collapse Reach a Black Hole’s Extreme Limit?
item.description:
Read the 2026-11-27 edition

  • Can Collapse Reach a Black Hole’s Extreme Limit? — A mathematical construction shows uncharged matter forming an exactly extremal black hole in finite time, challenging a version of black-hole thermodynamics’ third law.
  • Could Dark Matter Cool the Gas Around M87’s Black Hole? — A proposed test treats hot infalling gas as a thermometer for light dark matter, then compares its predicted radio-to-millimeter glow with observations.
  • How Tall Is a Neutron Star’s Accretion Shock? — Four relativistic simulations offer geometric estimates for intensely fed neutron stars, but translating a modeled column into an X-ray spectral fit remains an interpretive step.
  • Do Waveform Models Invent Clues to Black Hole Origins? — A simulation study finds that model choice can shift some individual measurements, while population-level spin–mass patterns remain broadly recoverable at current design sensitivity.
  • The Researchers Behind a Faster Gravitational-Wave Alert — A far-flung team’s publication trail runs from pulsar searches and sky-localization methods to the practical challenge of telling other astronomers where—and what—to look for.

item.title: The Darkstar — 2026-11-26: New Study Maps Curvature in Active Galaxy Jets, Probing Black Hole Dynamics
item.description:
Read the 2026-11-26 edition

  • New Study Maps Curvature in Active Galaxy Jets, Probing Black Hole Dynamics — Researchers identify hundreds of active galactic nuclei with bent jets, offering new statistical insights into the complex physics of supermassive black hole systems and their outflows.
  • Stellar Evolution's Hidden Hand in Black Hole Mass Gap Mystery — New research explores how stellar properties like metallicity and rotation influence the maximum mass of black holes, potentially resolving a conflict with gravitational-wave observations.
  • Future Gravitational-Wave Detectors Face Challenges in Unlocking Neutron Star Post-Merger Secrets — A new analysis explores the prospects for detecting the faint, high-frequency gravitational waves from the aftermath of binary neutron star collisions, highlighting the differing sensitivities to population-wide signals versus individual events.
  • How a radio team grew around the Irish LOFAR telescope — The Crab survey is the latest chapter in a collaboration that had already built data tools, tracked intermittent neutron stars and measured how plasma distorts pulsar signals.
